note: Study skeleton paraphrased from the course scope (not verbatim College Board prose; unit numbers are our own sequencing, not official CED numbers). Skill codes are indicative: 1.x concept, 2.x/3.x skill.

objectives.statement: Explain the Articles' failures, federalism, and separation of powers with checks and balances.
Analyze how federalism creates tension and cooperation between levels of government.
Explain lawmaking, committees, and the incumbency advantage.
Trace how a bill becomes law and where it can stall.
Explain formal and informal executive powers and how the bureaucracy implements policy.
Evaluate presidential influence over domestic and foreign policy.
Explain Marbury v. Madison, judicial review, and how courts make policy.
Analyze how precedent and ideology shape Supreme Court decisions.
Explain the Bill of Rights, selective incorporation, and landmark equality cases.
Apply the 14th Amendment to evaluate government action on rights.
Explain voting behavior, parties, interest groups, and media influence.
Analyze why turnout varies and how groups convert resources into influence.
Explain the Electoral College and differences between primary and general campaigns.
Evaluate how campaign finance, polling, and media shape election outcomes.
